context.guidance: Give each Data Principal a route to correct, complete or update every user-editable Personal Data Element, and apply the change in every store the value lives in, including caches and derived records. §12(2) provides the right to correction, completion and update, and Rule 14 sets how the Data Principal exercises it.

value.fix: Make updateUserProfile a complete correction route under DPDP §12(2) and Rule 14, so the Data Principal can correct, complete or update every personal data element they're allowed to edit. The visible code only looks up the user by loggedInUser.data.id, so it doesn't yet show that every field can be changed or that changes reach every store. (1) Accept and validate each editable field, not just username. Use a strict allow-list such as username, email, profileImage and other contact details. Reject unknown fields, check formats and uniqueness (for example, email), and never let role, id, isActive, totpSecret or the password hash be changed through this route. (2) Look up the user only by the authenticated identity, as the code already does, and require CSRF protection or a same-site check. (3) Save the changes inside a database transaction, and in the same transaction update every derived or copied record that holds the old value. Examples are stored copies of the email or username in reviews, complaints, feedback, orders, deliveries, addresses and memories. Where possible, change those records to point to the user ID instead of keeping their own copy. (4) Update the caches: replace the security.authenticatedUsers entry for the current token, issue a new JWT with the corrected claims via security.authorize(updatedUser), set the new token cookie, and invalidate any other active sessions or cached profile and token data, so no old value keeps being served. (5) Return the updated profile so the user can confirm the change was applied. Record the correction request and its result for Rule 14 accountability. Reply within the required timeframe, and if a field can't be changed, tell the user why. (6) Add tests showing that each editable field can be corrected, that the change appears in the database, the session cache, the reissued token and all derived records, and that protected fields can't be changed.
